subject: Re: MedSys DPA – handling of LLM outputs, no-train option and onshore processing
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medsys.io>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medsys.io>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: DPA questions: training, outputs and subprocessors

Hi David,

Thanks for the demo last week — MedSys is excited about the latency profile and the routing options. Before we proceed to procurement, our legal and security teams have a few specific asks for the DPA and SOW:

- A firm "no-training" commitment for our tenant data (we need a clause that says our prompts/responses will not be used to improve models).
- Clarification that outputs generated by the model (responses, summaries) are licensed to MedSys and that Redwood will not claim ownership or derivative rights.
- Confirmation of subprocessors and whether any processing occurs outside the US; if so, we need onshore-only options and KMS residency.
- Evidence pack: SOC 2 report, subprocessor list, and a short dataflow diagram showing where customer content may be cached or persisted.

Attached is our initial ask list — procurement will follow with a redline if the legal language is acceptable. Can you confirm what positions Redwood can take here and any constraints for a hosted vs. private deployment?

Best,
Elena Rossi
Director, Privacy & Compliance
MedSys Health

Subject: Re: DPA questions: training, outputs and subprocessors

Hi Elena — thanks for laying this out clearly. Short answers up front: we can support a contractual no-training commitment and explicit customer ownership of outputs; the exact operational evidence and residency model depends on the deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

High level:
- No-training (opt-out): Available as a contractual option. For Hosted customers we provide an operational isolation profile and a contractual obligation not to use tenant data for model improvement, but we do retain some short-lived telemetry for debugging (covered in the DPA). For Dedicated/Private deployments we can offer stronger operational guarantees (no shared model improvements, onshore KMS, and configurable retention).
- Outputs/IP: We have standard DPA language that grants customers ownership or a perpetual license to outputs; Redwood does not assert derivative rights over customer prompts/responses under that language.
- Subprocessors & residency: We publish a subprocessor list and can discuss onshore processing for customer data in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, some edge caching may be routed through regional CDN or inference nodes — we can provide a residency map and SFTP export options.

I've looped in Neha (privacy/legal) and Vanessa (CS/onboarding). Neha — can you share the redlined clause we typically propose for the no-training opt-out and the evidence pack timeline? Vanessa — once we align on the clause, can you own the artifact collection for MedSys?

I attached a concise suggested clause (redline) to get the contract discussion started. Happy to hop on a call this week with legal/procurement.

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: DPA questions: training, outputs and subprocessors

Hi Elena and David,

Thanks — tagging a few specifics from the privacy/legal side. I've pasted proposed contractual language below (extract) and a short plan for evidence:

Proposed extract (for DPA / Annex):
"Customer Data" shall mean any data, prompts, inputs and content provided by Customer to Redwood for the purpose of invoking the Service. Redwood agrees that it will not utilize Customer Data to improve or retrain any of Redwood's models or models developed by third parties, whether by direct training, fine-tuning, or inclusion in model improvement pipelines, except where Customer has given explicit, documented consent. Redwood further agrees that Customer retains all rights in and to Outputs and any derivatives thereof generated from Customer Data.

Operational notes:
- Hosted: We can commit contractually to the above language. Operationally, Hosted retains limited telemetry and aggregated metrics; we will exclude Customer Data from any internal model improvement pipelines. We will provide a signed attestation and SOC 2 report, plus a sanitized dataflow diagram.
- Dedicated / Private: We can offer stronger isolation (no telemetry export, KMS residency options, and on-premises control path) — this is the recommended option if MedSys requires absolute operational segregation.

Evidence & timeline we can deliver:
- Current SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) — 3 business days after NDA for procurement.
- Up-to-date subprocessor registry & commitments — 1 business day.
- Short dataflow diagram of request/response lifecycle and KV/prefix caching practices (see attached).
- Signed no-training attestation for contract (we'll prepare once language is agreed).

A few caveats to flag (so procurement/legal can see constraints):
- If MedSys requires full-proof-of-no-copy in Hosted (i.e., zero-copy at all infrastructure layers), we typically move customers to Dedicated/Private due to shared control plane and telemetry needs on Hosted.
- Onshore KMS for Hosted is limited; Dedicated/Private can support customer-managed keys in a US-only region.

If useful, I can join a legal-to-legal call next week.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Hi Neha/David,

Please find attached our redline of the DPA and a short cover note. Two practical follow-ups we need confirmation on before legal will sign:

1) Retention: we requested a 30-day maximum for transient request logs and a 90-day maximum for aggregated telemetry. Can Redwood commit to those maxima (or propose practical minima)?
2) Export controls & backups: we need assurance that backups that may contain Customer Data will not be transferred outside the US. If Redwood uses any cross-border backups for Hosted, we need a mitigation plan or confirmation that backups are US-only for our tenant.

Hi team — quick update and proposed next steps: 

- Retention: For Hosted we can guarantee transient request logs retention <= 45 days by default; however, for MedSys' requirement of <=30 days we recommend Dedicated/Private where retention windows are configurable and contractually enforceable. For aggregated telemetry we can agree to a 90-day maximum in the DPA.
- Backups/exports: For Hosted, some cross-region backups exist for disaster recovery; we can provide a backup residency carve-out for MedSys by placing you on a US-only backup tier in Dedicated or Private. For Hosted customers that cannot accept cross-border backups, Dedicated/Private is the recommended path.

Operational proposal: Redwood will prepare a DPA mark incorporating the no-training extract Neha provided and the following options in the SOW: (A) Hosted with contractual no-training + attestation + 45d log retention (B) Dedicated with onshore KMS and configurable retention incl. 30d log retention (C) Private on-prem package. Please confirm which option MedSys prefers; we can then finalize the redline in 3 business days.

I'll also open a HubSpot task and assign onboarding artifacts. Vanessa — can you coordinate the evidence pack delivery once MedSys confirms the path?

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

1) Confirm deployment preference (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
2) Signed NDA (if not already executed) to release SOC 2 Type II report.
3) Procurement to confirm retention windows selection (Hosted: 45d default or Dedicated: custom 30d).
4) DocuSign-ready DPA + redline acceptance.
5) Access requested: engineering contact + IP allowlist + SFTP location for exports if needed.
6) Onshore KMS: if MedSys selects Dedicated/Private, provide KMS ownership requirements and region.
